The CSS change itself is plausible but unproven — nobody has confirmed the header actually shrinks on a real render.

Requirement #2's fallback ("if time runs short, ship step 1 only and leave step 2 as a To-do line in ext/Doc's readme") wasn't followed either: public/framework/ext/Doc/readme.md has no line about the title-as-switcher idea. A reader of the readme has no trace that step 2 was ever asked for or deferred.

Doc.css:50-62 carries an explicit 2026-09-29 design note arguing the tab bar should WRAP rather than scroll, citing "persistent navigation never moves or hides" as the reason it deliberately overrides ext/tabs' own nowrap+scroll default. The new mobile rule (Doc.css:20-32) reinstates exactly that nowrap+scroll behavior below 600px, which the owner's own requirements.md explicitly asks for — so it's the right call, but the old comment block now reads as contradicted and should probably get a line pointing at the new one so the next reader doesn't think the mobile fix is an oversight.

No check_page (or any other render check) run shows in this task's files — only the diff and a brief skill-loading log. Worth confirming the page still boots and the header doesn't visually break before this merges.

findings.text: Does what requirements.md step 1 asked: below 600px the Doc tab-bar (`public/framework/ext/Doc/Doc.css:38-50`) now scrolls one line sideways instead of wrapping to a second/third row — confirmed by `shots/before-dictate-400.png` vs `after-dictate-400.png` (two tab rows collapse to one, content starts noticeably higher) and the logged pixel measurement (122px → 85px, task.jsonl line 9). `shots/before-view-400.png`/`after-view-400.png` show no regression on a module whose tabs already fit one line, and `after-dictate-1200.png` shows desktop untouched.

Step 2 (title-as-switcher) was correctly parked under budget with a To-do line in `public/framework/ext/Doc/readme.md` naming the owner's own phrasing ("Dictate · Overview ▾") and linking this task, matching requirement #2's fallback instruction exactly.

The older 2026-09-29 comment at `Doc.css:50-62` arguing tabs should wrap, not scroll, now has a cross-reference (diff lines 10-15) pointing at the new `@media` block and explaining why the trade flips below 600px — so a future reader won't read the new rule as contradicting that note by accident.

No `check_page` run or render-check is recorded in task.jsonl/files.jsonl, and the branch (`worktree/mobile-doc-header`) is still unmerged. CLAUDE.md's review gate wants the four widths (400/1200/1920/3440) checked and `merge.mjs` run before this lands — worth a last look at 1920/3440 (not shot here) since only 400 and 1200 were captured, even though the change is scoped to `width <= 600px` and can't affect those widths by construction.

Simplicity: this reuses `ext/tabs`' own default nowrap+scroll behavior (already written, already proven on every other tab strip on the site) rather than inventing a new mobile pattern — the CSS added is ~10 lines, which is about as small as this fix gets.
